questions.question: During a site audit, the inspector points out that the site's PQS lacks an element of ICH Q10 that goes "beyond current regional GMP requirements". According to the introduction of ICH Q10, how should this gap be viewed?

options.A: A major deficiency, because Q10 has replaced the regional GMP regulations and the provisions beyond GMP must be adopted in full
options.B: Optional content, because Q10 is not intended to create any new expectations beyond current regulatory requirements
options.C: Mandatory content, because Q10 sets additional compulsory provisions for marketed products to meet new requirements specific to biologics
options.D: Mandatory content, applicable as long as the site's products are biologics

questions.explanation: Section 1.1 states explicitly that ICH Q10 is not intended to create any new expectations beyond current regulatory requirements, so the content of Q10 that goes beyond regional GMP is optional. Q10 is a model to be used together with regional GMP (section 1.3), not a replacement for GMP; it sets no separate mandatory provisions for marketed products or biologics, and its scope already covers biological products.

questions.question: Which of the following activities is NOT within the scope of the product lifecycle technical activities defined by ICH Q10?

options.A: Technology transfer of a marketed product between manufacturing and testing sites
options.B: Manufacture of investigational products
options.C: Retention of samples and continued product assessment after product discontinuation
options.D: Distribution activities of a wholesaler

questions.explanation: Section 1.2 lists Distribution as part of Commercial Manufacturing but explicitly notes "excluding wholesaler activities". Technology transfer includes transfers of marketed products between sites; Pharmaceutical Development includes the manufacture of investigational products; Product Discontinuation includes document retention, sample retention, and continued product assessment.

questions.question: A company establishes a system for monitoring and controlling process performance and product quality, with the aim of ensuring the continued suitability and capability of its processes. Which ICH Q10 objective does this mainly correspond to?

options.A: Establish and Maintain a State of Control
options.B: Achieve Product Realisation, which focuses on delivering a product that meets patient and regulatory needs
options.C: Facilitate Continual Improvement, which focuses on identifying and prioritizing areas that need improvement
options.D: Reduce the number of regulatory submissions in all regions

questions.explanation: Section 1.5.2 states that the state-of-control objective is to develop and use effective monitoring and control systems for process performance and product quality, thereby providing assurance of continued process suitability and capability. Product realisation (1.5.1) focuses on delivering a product with quality attributes that meet the needs of patients and regulators; continual improvement (1.5.3) focuses on identifying and implementing improvements. Reducing the number of submissions is not among the Q10 objectives.

questions.question: Which statement about the two ICH Q10 enablers (knowledge management and quality risk management) is correct?

options.A: They are one of the four PQS elements, listed alongside CAPA and change management
options.B: They apply only to the commercial manufacturing stage and are not needed during development
options.C: KM is the systematic acquisition, analysis, storage, and dissemination of information; QRM provides a proactive approach to identifying, scientifically evaluating, and controlling risks
options.D: KM is responsible for evaluating risk, and QRM is responsible for storing and disseminating product information

questions.explanation: Section 1.6 explains that KM and QRM are enablers that help achieve the objectives in section 1.5 and apply throughout the product lifecycle (Annex 2 also states that they apply to all stages). KM is defined as the systematic approach to acquiring, analysing, storing, and disseminating information (1.6.1); QRM is the proactive identification, scientific evaluation, and control of potential quality risks (1.6.2). The four PQS elements are monitoring, CAPA, change management, and management review (3.2) and do not include the enablers; the roles of the two also cannot be swapped.

questions.question: According to ICH Q10, which of the following does the quality manual (or an equivalent documentation approach) describing the PQS NOT need to include?

options.A: The content of the batch production record for each batch of product
options.B: The quality policy and the scope of the PQS
options.C: The PQS processes, as well as their sequences, linkages, and interdependencies
options.D: Management responsibilities within the PQS

questions.explanation: Section 1.8 specifies that the quality manual should include the quality policy, the scope of the PQS, the identification of the PQS processes (including their sequences, linkages, and interdependencies, which can be supported by process maps and flow charts), and management responsibilities. The batch production record is a product-level operational document and is not part of the quality manual's description of the PQS.

questions.question: A site quality head says, "Quality is the QA department's business; senior management only needs to approve the budget." According to ICH Q10 section 2.1, what is wrong with this statement?

options.A: Nothing is wrong; Q10 states that quality responsibility belongs only to an independent quality unit
options.B: Nothing is wrong; management responsibility is limited to the commercial manufacturing stage
options.C: Senior management has ultimate responsibility for ensuring an effective PQS is in place, and must be involved in its design, implementation, and monitoring
options.D: It is wrong, because senior management should replace the quality unit in exercising release authority

questions.explanation: Section 2.1, item a states that senior management has ultimate responsibility for ensuring that an effective PQS is in place to achieve the quality objectives; item b requires management to participate in the design, implementation, monitoring, and maintenance of the PQS and to demonstrate strong and visible support. An independent quality unit is required by regional regulations, but this does not relieve senior management of responsibility; Q10 also does not require senior management to replace the quality unit, and management responsibility applies at all lifecycle stages (Annex 2).

questions.question: A company outsources aseptic filling to a CMO and has signed a written agreement. When a quality problem occurs, who is ultimately responsible according to ICH Q10?

options.A: The commissioning pharmaceutical company remains ultimately responsible for ensuring that the outsourced activities are controlled
options.B: The CMO that accepts the work, because the party doing the actual operation bears full responsibility, and the company is responsible only if the two parties agree otherwise
options.C: Both parties share it equally, regardless of the content of the agreement, and responsibility transfers automatically with the signed contract
options.D: It is decided by the regulatory authority, and the company only needs to cooperate

questions.explanation: Section 2.7 states that the PQS and management responsibility extend to the control and review of outsourced activities and the quality of purchased materials, and that the pharmaceutical company is ultimately responsible. The written agreement is used to define the responsibilities and communication processes of both parties (2.7, item b) and does not transfer ultimate responsibility; Q10 also does not provide that the regulatory authority allocates responsibility.

questions.question: Which of the following is consistent with ICH Q10 requirements for the quality policy?

options.A: It only needs to be kept by the quality department and need not be explained to general staff, and need not be updated even if its content has been understood by every department
options.B: Once established it stays unchanged to ensure consistency, and is kept confidential to prevent it from leaking outside
options.C: Its content only needs to cover product release criteria and need not mention regulations
options.D: It is communicated to and understood by personnel at all levels, and is periodically reviewed for continuing effectiveness

questions.explanation: Section 2.2 requires senior management to establish a quality policy; the policy should include an expectation to comply with applicable regulatory requirements and promote continual improvement of the PQS, must be communicated to and understood by personnel at all levels of the company, and should be periodically reviewed for continuing effectiveness. Therefore "known only to the quality department", "never revised", or "no mention of regulations" all contradict the text.

questions.question: A company acquires a marketed product from another company. According to ICH Q10 section 2.8, which two things should management ensure?

options.A: Stop the product immediately and repeat all validation, with other information supplied later
options.B: Define the continuing responsibilities of each company involved, and transfer the necessary information
options.C: Destroy all quality records, to be rebuilt by the new company, which re-establishes all processes
options.D: Only update the name of the marketing authorization holder; nothing else needs to be done

questions.explanation: Section 2.8 provides that when product ownership changes (for example, through acquisition), management should consider its complexity and ensure that item a: the ongoing responsibilities of each company involved are defined and item b: the necessary information is transferred. The text does not require stopping production, repeating all validation, or destroying records, and merely changing the name would not cover the responsibilities and information transfer.

questions.question: According to ICH Q10 quality planning (section 2.3), which of the following is the correct approach to quality objectives?

options.A: They are set independently by the quality department without support from other levels, with each department setting its own without coordinating with the others
options.B: They are re-set only after a major deviation, and are unrelated to the company's overall strategy
options.C: They focus on after-the-fact recording and need no performance indicators
options.D: They are aligned with company strategies and consistent with the quality policy, and progress is measured with performance indicators

questions.explanation: Section 2.3 requires senior management to ensure that quality objectives are defined and communicated; the objectives must be supported by all relevant levels of the company, aligned with company strategies, and consistent with the quality policy; management must provide appropriate resources and training; and performance indicators are established to measure progress, which are regularly monitored and communicated, with action taken as needed (see also section 4.1).

questions.question: A site's monitoring system collects only in-house in-process control data. According to ICH Q10 section 3.2.1, what is this system missing?

options.A: Only daily output statistics need to be added; nothing else is needed, and trend analysis is left to suppliers to carry out and interpret
options.B: Only certificates of analysis from suppliers, used as the sole basis for judging the state of control of the process
options.C: Only clinical trial data from the new drug development stage, needed only when requested by a customer and then evaluated
options.D: Product quality feedback from internal and external sources, such as complaints, returns, recalls, audits, and regulatory inspection findings

questions.explanation: Section 3.2.1, item e requires the monitoring system to include feedback on product quality from both internal and external sources, such as complaints, product rejections, non-conformances, recalls, deviations, audits, and regulatory inspections and findings. The other options do not fit: the monitoring system is for providing assurance of a state of control during commercial manufacturing, and clinical trial results are an out-of-scope input (3.1.1).

questions.question: There are two investigations: a major deviation affecting the release of multiple lots of a sterile product, and a low-risk documentation typo. According to the ICH Q10 CAPA system, how should the investigations be conducted?

options.A: Both must follow exactly the same full investigation process, to remain consistent
options.B: Both need a structured investigation to find the root cause, but the level of effort, formality, and documentation depend on the risk
options.C: The low-risk event needs no investigation or record and is simply corrected
options.D: Only the major deviation needs a root cause to be found; the other is simply closed

questions.explanation: Section 3.2.2 states that a structured approach to the investigation should be used, with the aim of determining the root cause, and that the level of effort, formality, and documentation of the investigation should be commensurate with the level of risk, consistent with ICH Q9. It is therefore neither always identical nor exempt from investigation when the risk is low.

questions.question: A process change is made entirely within the approved design space. According to ICH Q10 section 3.2.3, how should this change be handled?

options.A: No internal evaluation or record is needed, because it is within the approved range
options.B: Regulatory approval must always be sought before implementation
options.C: It is not considered a change from a regulatory filing perspective, but from the PQS standpoint it must still be evaluated by the change management system
options.D: Verbal agreement from the quality unit alone is sufficient

questions.explanation: Section 3.2.3, item b refers to ICH Q8: working within the design space is not considered a change (as regards regulatory filings), but from a PQS standpoint, all changes should be evaluated by a company's change management system. Evaluation therefore cannot be skipped, and approval of a submission is not always required.

questions.question: According to ICH Q10 Table II, how should CAPA be applied in the Product Discontinuation stage?

options.A: CAPA should continue, taking into account the impact on the product remaining on the market and on other products that might be affected
options.B: Once the product is discontinued, CAPA can all be closed, and there is no need to consider products still in circulation on the market
options.C: CAPA is first initiated only at the product discontinuation stage, because data from the development stage are irrelevant to it
options.D: CAPA only needs to address the exploration of variability in the new drug development stage

questions.explanation: Table II in section 3.2.2 states that after product discontinuation, CAPA should continue and the impact on the product remaining on the market, as well as on other products that might be affected, should be considered. In development, CAPA is used to explore variability and is fed into iterative design; in commercial manufacturing, the effectiveness of actions must be evaluated. CAPA therefore does not end at discontinuation.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the "internal and external factors" that management should monitor, as listed in ICH Q10 section 4.2?

options.A: The individual weight variation result of a single batch, with all judgments based mainly on after-the-fact review
options.B: Emerging regulations, guidances, and quality issues that can have an impact on the PQS
options.C: The CoA values of each incoming lot from a particular supplier, which the supplier is responsible for interpreting and reporting
options.D: The output achievement rate of a production line on a given day

questions.explanation: Section 4.2 lists the factors monitored by management: emerging regulations, guidances, and quality issues; innovations that might enhance the PQS; changes in business environment and objectives; and changes in product ownership. Single-batch data, CoA values, and output are routine operational matters, not PQS-level internal and external factors.

questions.question: According to the ICH Q10 glossary (citing ISO 9000:2005), what is the difference between corrective action and preventive action?

options.A: Corrective action prevents recurrence; preventive action prevents occurrence
options.B: Corrective action prevents occurrence; preventive action prevents recurrence, so the two are actually the same action described differently
options.C: Both are used only for non-conformities that have already occurred and there is no difference, applying only to supplier non-conformities
options.D: Corrective action targets suppliers; preventive action targets internal processes

questions.explanation: The glossary notes that corrective action is action to eliminate the cause of a detected non-conformity and is used to prevent recurrence, whereas preventive action is action to eliminate the cause of a potential non-conformity and is used to prevent occurrence. The incorrect options swap the two, say there is no difference, or distinguish them by target, all of which contradict the definitions.

questions.question: According to the glossary, what is the definition of "State of Control"?

options.A: A state in which all batch test results fall within specification, and which is a prerequisite for pre-marketing approval
options.B: A state in which the process has been validated and no longer needs monitoring, with no need to maintain or review it once achieved
options.C: A condition in which the set of controls consistently provides assurance of continued process performance and product quality
options.D: A state in which the company has obtained approval from the regulatory authority

questions.explanation: The glossary defines State of Control as a condition in which the set of controls consistently provides assurance of continued process performance and product quality. It emphasizes continuing assurance, so "validated and no longer monitored" contradicts it; looking only at specification results or at obtaining approval is also not part of the definition.

questions.question: According to Annex 1, when a company demonstrates both an effective PQS and product and process understanding (scenario 4), which potential opportunity is specifically listed in addition to the others?

options.A: Maintaining compliance only (status quo)
options.B: Optimized science- and risk-based post-approval change processes to facilitate innovation and continual improvement
options.C: Only an increased number of risk-based inspections, with no other opportunities
options.D: Only the establishment of a real-time release mechanism

questions.explanation: In Annex 1, scenario 1 (GMP compliance only) is just compliance - status quo; the opportunity in scenario 2 (effective PQS) is more risk-based inspections; scenario 3 (product and process understanding) offers science-based quality assessment, innovative validation, and real-time release; only scenario 4 additionally lists optimization of post-approval change processes. The Annex notes that the actual regulatory processes depend on the region.

questions.question: Which statement about the PQS model illustrated in ICH Q10 Annex 2 is correct?

options.A: The PQS replaces regional GMP and does not cover product discontinuation, and management responsibility applies only at the technology transfer stage
options.B: The enablers function only at the commercial manufacturing stage, and the enablers are used only in the product development stage
options.C: Management responsibility covers only the technology transfer stage
options.D: The PQS augments regional GMPs, and regional GMPs apply to the manufacture of investigational products

questions.explanation: Annex 2 explains that the PQS covers the whole lifecycle of development, technology transfer, commercial manufacturing, and product discontinuation; the PQS augments regional GMPs, and regional GMPs apply to the manufacture of investigational products; management responsibility applies at all stages; and the enablers (knowledge management and QRM) apply across all lifecycle stages.

questions.question: According to the glossary, what is the definition of "Quality Objectives"?

options.A: The overall intentions and direction of a company related to quality as formally expressed by senior management, reviewed only at the annual management review
options.B: The minimum regulatory acceptance criteria set for deciding on action, used as the legal basis for approving a marketing application
options.C: A means to translate the quality policy and strategies into measurable activities
options.D: Measurements used to quantify performance, also called performance indicators

questions.explanation: The glossary defines Quality Objectives as a means to translate the quality policy and strategies into measurable activities. The first distractor is actually the definition of Quality Policy; the last is the definition of Performance Indicators (measurable values used to quantify quality objectives to reflect performance); a regulatory minimum standard is not a glossary definition.
